values.note: $30 a night for drive-up tent, camper and motor home sites (walk-in tent $22, group tent $60), paid when reserving, not at the campground. An Acadia entrance pass is required while staying in the campground: $35 per vehicle. Non-US residents 16 and older also pay a $100 nonresident fee unless admitted with an Annual or America the Beautiful pass.

fees.source: https://www.nps.gov/acad/planyourvisit/seawall-campground.htm ('Drive-up tent, camper, and motor home sites: $30') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/234674/rates (season 2026-05-20 to 2026-10-11: RV NONELECTRIC 30) + the facility's notices on https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/234674 ('An entrance pass is required in the park and while staying in the campground ... $35 per vehicle'), read 2026-11-02

values.note: All sites by reservation on recreation.gov; none at the office or in person. 90% of sites are released six months ahead on the first of each month at 10 am Eastern, the other 10% at 10 am 14 days ahead of arrival, rolling; same-day reservations if sites are open. Combined limit of 14 nights in Acadia campgrounds between the Friday of Memorial Day weekend and Columbus Day, 30 nights per calendar year. Check-in after noon, check-out before 10 am.

booking.source: https://www.nps.gov/acad/planyourvisit/seawall-campground.htm + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/234674 (Overview, facility_rules reservationWindow 6 months, maxConsecutiveStay 14, notices), read 2026-11-02

values.note: 'open seasonally, typically from the Wednesday before Memorial Day to Columbus Day'. NPS's page still gives the 2025 dates, May 21 through Oct 13; recreation.gov's 2026 rate season ran May 20 to Oct 11.

season.source: https://developer.nps.gov/api/v1/campgrounds?parkCode=acad (Seawall operatingHours) + https://www.nps.gov/acad/planyourvisit/seawall-campground.htm ('Season Dates: May 21 through Oct 13, 2025'), read 2026-11-02

hookups.source: https://developer.nps.gov/api/v1/campgrounds?parkCode=acad (electricalHookups 0) + recreation.gov catalog (every site type NONELECTRIC or walk-to), read 2026-11-02

values.note: Of 202 sites only Loop C's 30 RV sites list 30 or 35 ft; Loop A's 20 RV-permitted sites and C15, C33 list 20 ft. The rest are walk-to or tent-only. NPS gives a 20-ft maximum, explaining it by the tight turn of the A-Loop road. One vehicle per site, all equipment on the pad. Generators only in Loop C, 8-10 am and 4-7 pm.

sites.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/234674 ('some sites can accommodate RVs up to 35 ft'; 'Generators may only be used in Loop C') + its campsite catalog (trip_data/ridb_campsites.json, fetched 2026-10-20) + https://developer.nps.gov/api/v1/campgrounds?parkCode=acad (totalSites 202; rvMaxLength 20), read 2026-11-02

values.note: No showers in the campground (portable showers prohibited); private pay showers less than a mile away. Cell coverage is poor.

facilities.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/234674 ('Flush toilets, running water and a dump station are provided'; 'No showers') + https://www.nps.gov/acad/planyourvisit/seawall-campground.htm, read 2026-11-02

summary: Confirmed $30 drive-up RV sites (2026 rec.gov rate table + NPS), no hookups, dump, flush toilets, no showers, 6-month rec.gov windows. Added $35 Acadia entrance fee, booking, season, 202 sites, 35-ft max (Loop C only). Note kept verbatim.

So Route 102A and the Seawall picnic area lie between the sites and the shore. AWH's own note says the sites 'are not waterfront'. I read this as not waterfront. This is a revisit under the 2026-11-02 'no separate pass' line.
